reconcile.connective: Commentators read the "sword" as the social division Jesus's call for allegiance provokes, distinct from the spiritual peace promised in John 14:27.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the objection bluntly: the peacemaking Jesus of Matthew 5 cannot be squared with Matthew 10:34's "not peace, but a sword."

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is Jesus peaceful?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/sword.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is Jesus peaceful?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/sword.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Jesus did bring peace (John 14:27), but not of a social and political kind. Instead, Jesus calls humans to make a decision about him, which brings a sword—i.e., division (see Matt 8:21-22; 12:46-50; Luke 12:51).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles the Matt 10:34 sword saying with the John 14:27 peace saying by distinguishing social/political peace from relational peace with God, and cross-references Luke 12:51.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's table 'Mission: Peace / War' pairs Isaiah 9:6 and John 14:27 against Matthew 10:34-36 directly, resolving it as peace being the object of Christ's mission with strife only an incidental, not contradictory, result (p. 118-119).
